note: Practice pack: 11+ vocabulary tasks with fixed answers. Generic content - contains no personal information.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to waste money or time when you really shouldn't'?
tasks.teach: To squander pocket money is to blow it all in one go — the show-off opposite of saving.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to tempt someone with something lovely'?
tasks.teach: The smell of warm cookies can entice anyone into the kitchen. Tempt, attract, entice — all magnets!

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to officially say NO to a plan'?
tasks.teach: 'Permit' means allow — veto is its bossy opposite: one powerful NO that blocks the plan.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to stop completely'?
tasks.teach: When rain ceases, it stops. 'Cease' is a posh full stop — and 'commence' kicks things off.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'a huge, noisy crowd'?
tasks.teach: A horde of fans mobbed the stage! (Sneaky cousin: 'hoard' with an A is treasure you keep.)

tasks.prompt: The moon grew smaller every night — it had started to ___.
tasks.teach: Waxing adds light, waning takes it away — like a candle slowly going out.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to keep going through something hard without giving up'?
tasks.teach: Explorers endure freezing nights — they grit their teeth and carry on. You endure a very long queue!

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'looking down and feeling gloomy'?
tasks.teach: Downcast eyes stare at shoes. 'Jaunty' is the happy opposite — chin up, cap at an angle!

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to get in the way and slow someone down'?
tasks.teach: A pebble in your shoe hinders a runner. Its rhyme-twin 'hamper' means exactly the same!

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to run with quick little steps, like a squirrel'?
tasks.teach: Squirrels scamper, tired hikers trudge. The word sounds as quick as the feet!

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'happening once every year'?
tasks.teach: Your birthday is annual — once a year ('annus' is Latin for year, like in 'anniversary').

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'a tiny flying insect that loves to bite on summer evenings'?
tasks.teach: Midges are the itchy dots of summer. (A larva is a baby insect, a drake is a boy duck, an ermine is a stoat — collect all four!)

tasks.prompt: Word detective! Which ONE word fits BOTH clues: 'a harbour for ships' AND 'the left side of a boat'?
tasks.teach: Port is the harbour AND the boat's left side. One word, two jobs — English loves a doubler.

tasks.prompt: Word detective! Which ONE word fits BOTH clues: 'a long story book' AND 'completely new and original'?
tasks.teach: You can read a novel, and invent a novel idea — same word, two meanings.

tasks.prompt: A 'plight' is...
tasks.teach: The knight rescued the villagers from their plight — their sticky situation.

tasks.prompt: Someone 'nimble' is...
options: quick and light on their feet
tasks.answer: quick and light on their feet
tasks.teach: Jack be nimble, Jack be quick! Gymnasts and squirrels: nimble.

tasks.prompt: A 'cryptic' message is...
tasks.teach: Cryptic = puzzling, hidden. To decipher a cryptic note is to crack its code — detective work!

tasks.prompt: 'Vast' means...
tasks.teach: The Sahara is vast, space is vaster. Huge, immense, enormous — vast's word family.

tasks.prompt: Your 'visage' is your...
tasks.teach: A knight's grim visage = his stern face. Fancy word, simple meaning — examiners love it.

tasks.prompt: The kitten was so ___ that it crept along the fence without a single wobble.
tasks.teach: Nimble = light and quick. Cumbersome is the clumsy opposite — imagine a piano on that fence.

tasks.prompt: The sky turned a brilliant ___ over the summer sea.
tasks.teach: Azure = bright sky-blue. A painter's word — it makes a sentence glow.

tasks.prompt: The old oak's ___ branches twisted like a witch's fingers.
tasks.teach: Gnarled = twisted and knobbly. Perfect for old trees, old roots, and wizard's hands.

tasks.prompt: She was so ___ that she practised every single day until the trick worked.
tasks.teach: Persistent = keeping at it, not giving up. The superpower behind every skill you've ever learned.

tasks.prompt: Three of these pull you closer. Which one pushes you away?
tasks.teach: Entice, tempt and attract are magnets — deter is the force field that stops you.

tasks.prompt: Which word is the odd one out?
tasks.teach: Vast, enormous and immense are giants — dainty is small and delicate, like a fairy's teacup.

tasks.prompt: Which word is the odd one out?
tasks.teach: Cease, halt and stop all slam the brakes — commence starts the engine!

tasks.prompt: If you 'smell a rat', you...
tasks.teach: No actual rats involved! Idioms mean more than their words — this one means 'something fishy is going on'. (Also fishy! English, honestly.)

tasks.prompt: Someone 'sitting on the fence' is...
tasks.teach: Can't pick a side? You're on the fence — one leg each way, deciding nothing.

tasks.prompt: Fix this sentence: The explorer couldn't bare the freezing wind.
tasks.answer: The explorer couldn't bear the freezing wind.
tasks.teach: To bear = to put up with (like a tough old bear). Bare = uncovered — bare feet in the snow, brrr!

tasks.prompt: Fix this sentence: Don't loose hope — the rescue ship is close!
tasks.answer: Don't lose hope — the rescue ship is close!
tasks.teach: Lose = can't find it / don't win. Loose = wobbly-tooth wobbly. One O of difference!

tasks.prompt: Fix this sentence: Your going to love this ancient castle.
tasks.answer: You're going to love this ancient castle.
tasks.teach: You're = you are (the apostrophe hides the missing A). Your = belonging to you, as in your crown.

tasks.prompt: Fix this sentence: The treasure was buried to deep too dig up.
tasks.answer: The treasure was buried too deep to dig up.
tasks.teach: Too = 'more than enough' (too deep, too late). To = direction or a to-do. This one had them swapped!

tasks.prompt: Designer challenge: invent a Word Zoo! Every new word you beat becomes a creature you collect. What do they look like? Where do they live? You decide — sketch it, then build it!
tasks.teach: Your game, your rules. (A 'menagerie' is a collection of animals — maybe your first exhibit?)
